header.allocation: 0x82533DB8 requests 52 bytes through 0x82465E18 before the helper chain writes the header.
header.builder: 0x826B6FE8 forwards r4/r5, maps the depth-one predicate, and carries the output pointers to 0x826B6D68; 0x826B6D68 passes the extent and selector values into 0x8269A378 and copies exactly 52 bytes into the header.
header.baseFields: 0x826B7140 adds the primary page base to header +0x20 and, when the descriptor count exceeds one, the second page base to +0x30 while preserving low 12 bits.

factoryConstantEffects: Factory r6=1 makes the creator depth-one predicate false after helper inversion, so builder mode receives zero in its corresponding control input.
Factory r8=0 clears both creator flag tests; the header's low type nibble remains 3 and the optional flag bits are not selected by this callsite.
The creator may still receive a nonzero second backing size from the selector and extent calculations; its presence is not fixed by the factory constants alone.
creatorDataflow.selectorDomain: The accepted classifier body maps the lower-six-bit selector to numeric values 1, 2, or 4 for the ordinary ranges, with the exact exceptional values 39 and 44 writing 4 to the first output and 1 to the second. The numeric results are not named as public formats.

creatorCalls.size: computed secondary backing size when nonzero

lowerAllocator.flagBranch: 0x8280DAC0 tests attribute bit 31 (0x80000000) and branches to the heap wrapper 0x8281B4F0 only when that bit is clear. 0xBCFF0000 has bit 31 set, so the creator's backing goes through 0x8280DE40 and the import MmAllocatePhysicalMemoryEx at 0x82E92654.
lowerAllocator.physicalPath: For attributes with bit 31 set, 0x8280DAC0 selects a table word from attribute bits 28..29, uses an alignment of 1 << (attribute bits 24..27) with the field defaulting to 0xC when it is clear, and calls 0x8280DE40, which calls MmAllocatePhysicalMemoryEx.
lowerAllocator.heapBranchNotTaken: The heap wrapper 0x8281B4F0 (heap selector 0x8, requested size forwarded to 0x82811658) serves attributes with bit 31 clear. It is not on the creator's backing path.
lowerAllocator.contents: Attribute bit 30 is clear for 0xBCFF0000, so 0x8280DAC0 does not call the zero-fill helper 0x827F7BB0 and the backing is not zero-filled by the allocator wrapper. The bounded creator/helper bodies visibly write descriptor/header words and contain no direct returned-range write; later texel writes are made under surface locks, so backing contents generation is not statically proved on this path.

lowerRelease.refcountBoundary: 0x82518678 decrements each retained resource's +0x04 atomically and calls 0x82518B40 only when the count reaches zero, then clears the slot. 0x82518E88 invokes this cleanup before the container teardown path.

classifier.creatorHeaderDomain: The creator header low nibble is 3. The classifier then reads header +0x30 bits 30..31; when that field is 1 it additionally tests header +0x20 bit 0x400 and a nested +0x18 resource word.
classifier.qualification: The high two bits of +0x30 can be changed by 0x826B7140 from the dynamic second backing page base, so the exact return value is not statically fixed by factory r6/r8 alone.

targetBodies.managerTargets: 0x825348A8, 0x82534950, and 0x825349F8 store the allocation attributes 0xBCFF0000, 0xBCFE0000, and 0xBCFD0000 into resource +0x04, append the header to the pending list at manager +0x22C under the lock at manager +0x208, and call 0x825325E0, whose bounded body updates a counted manager table with the resource pointer.
targetBodies.successStub: 0x82533D10 returns one and has no visible free or backing write.
targetBodies.deallocatorResult: None of the release targets frees the backing directly; they queue the header. The queued backing is freed by the deferred pass described in lowerRelease.deferredPass.

deferredPass.caller: renderer method 0x8250B8B0 calls renderer[0x574] slot +0x3C with r4 = renderer[0xA8]; the manager methods 0x82535E08, 0x82535F10, 0x82535880, and 0x82535C20 also call their own slot +0x3C after a failure test.
deferredPass.freeGate: A queued texture header is freed only when 0x826984D8 returns zero (not bound in the device stream, texture, index, or target tables) and 0x8269C738 returns zero (the fence block word has passed header +0x08).
deferredPass.frees: The primary page base (+0x20 & ~0xFFF) through 0x82E29160 with the attributes stored at +0x04; the secondary base (+0x30 & ~0xFFF) when it is nonzero, differs, and header +0x1C bit 0x00200000 is clear; then the header through 0x82465F08.
deferredPass.qualification: Static path only. How often the pass runs and how soon an address is reused are runtime facts.

identityAndReuse.allocationIdentity: unresolved; the allocator returns a pointer but no generation, owner token, or allocation record is joined to later cleanup.
identityAndReuse.contentsGeneration: unresolved; no backing-range fill or producer write is statically connected to the returned primary or secondary range inside the creator path.
identityAndReuse.addressRecycling: The deferred pass 0x82535298 frees the backing through MmFreePhysicalMemory, so a released range can return to the kernel allocator. Whether a later allocation reuses an earlier released address is unresolved; the bounded code does not correlate them.
identityAndReuse.containerOnlyFree: The destructor's flag path calls 0x82465DA8 with size 156 for the 0x9C-byte container; this is container teardown and does not prove backing-region release.

boundedNegative: The factory fixes creator r6=1 and r8=0 but leaves config words +0x00, +0x04, and +0x40 dynamic, so exact runtime width, height, selector, and derived sizes remain unresolved.

The lower classifier and device vtable targets are exact, but +0x30 high bits and the +0x20 control branch depend on dynamic backing and packed fields; no single lower release target is statically selected.

The exact lower release bodies queue the header or return success and do not free; the deferred pass 0x82535298 frees the backing. No allocation-generation field, contents producer, or address-reuse event is proved.
A readable pointer, descriptor snapshot, selector, or allocator attribute word is not an allocation-generation key.

runtimeDiscriminator.smallestDecisiveObservation: For the explicit-buffer path, one read-only record at pre-call boundary 0x82518608 should emit only r4, r5, r6, r7, r8 and the device vptr, with 0x8251860C retained only as the call continuation. One record at classifier call 0x82518B60 and post-call continuation 0x82518B64 should emit classifier code and selected device slot offset. Contents require bounded destination write tracking, and a lower-free observation is available at the two 0x82E29160 calls in the deferred pass 0x82535298. A reuse probe is admissible once a free is observed there.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only DumpFunctions.java, DumpMemoryWords.java, and DumpReferences.java queries against the canonical version-1.3 project, followed by exact generated-code windows for the factory, creator/helper chain, allocator dispatcher and physical allocator path, classifier, cleanup, destructor, release targets, and deferred release pass.

entries.result: A foreground read-only DumpFunctions.java query identified the exact function entries and caller/callee inventory used by this packet; target 0x82E29168 resolves to containing function 0x82AB9DE8, so its allocator-entry identity is supported by the generated tail-jump and the separate reference query rather than an exact DumpFunctions entry. Generated-code citations are retained only for bounded instruction bodies.
The explicit-buffer factory loads config +0x00, +0x04, and +0x40 into r4, r5, and r7, fixes r6=1 and r8=0, and dispatches device vtable +0x08; the continuation is not used as the input boundary.

entries.role: creator argument forwarding and allocation flags
entries.result: The creator forwards the five incoming words through the helper chain, requests one or two sizes, executes allocator instructions 0x82533E98 and 0x82533EB0 with continuations 0x82533E9C and 0x82533EB4, allocates both with 0xBCFF0000, and patches page bases into the header.

Refcount-zero cleanup reaches the classifier call at 0x82518B60 and post-call continuation 0x82518B64, then conditionally dispatches the accepted device vtable slots; the reachable target bodies queue the header for the deferred release pass 0x82535298.

Attribute bit 31 of 0xBCFF0000 is set, so the allocator takes the physical path 0x8280DE40 -> MmAllocatePhysicalMemoryEx 0x82E92654. The heap branch 0x8281B4F0 -> 0x82811658 serves attributes with bit 31 clear. The zero-fill helper 0x827F7BB0 is skipped because bit 30 is clear.

The release targets queue the header with its allocation attributes; 0x82535298 frees the backing through 0x82E29160 -> MmFreePhysicalMemory 0x82E92434 once the header is unbound and its fence has passed.

currentEvidence.qualification: Generated code is used only for exact functions selected from accepted anchors and narrow foreground queries. Static release and allocator paths do not establish runtime execution, pointer identity, contents, or reuse.

catalogPromotion.result: The exact explicit-buffer creator, factory, cleanup, lower classifier/dispatcher, allocator frontier, and conditional device release targets become reusable symbols and relations. The alternate factory 0x82517EC0 has a bounded runtime join to the shared creator but remains a separate input and ownership path. Dynamic input values, release selection, heap generation, contents production, and reuse remain explicitly qualified.

missingContracts.reason: The static path closes argument positions, allocator flags, classifier domain, device release targets, and the queue and deferred free, but the dynamic configuration words, backing addresses, contents writers, and temporal reuse relation are not selected.

guards: Do not call config +0x00 or +0x04 width and height by public name without a runtime or independent ABI discriminator.
Do not call config +0x40 a format or usage value without matching title dataflow beyond its classifier and packed-field roles.
Do not treat the release targets 0x825348A8, 0x82534950, and 0x825349F8 as the deallocator; they queue the header and the deferred pass 0x82535298 performs the free.
Do not treat a free-list position, header descriptor, page base, or allocator attribute word as allocation generation.

Do not treat the skipped zero-fill helper as proof that backing contents are initialized or GPU-complete; a contents observation requires bounded destination write tracking against transient returned-range tokens.

Do not apply this explicit-buffer input map or lower path to alternate factory 0x82517EC0, wrapper vtable 0x82047628, or creator-dispatch gate 0x82517FFC; the accepted alternate join proves the shared creator only and does not merge these paths.
Do not infer address reuse or allocation recycling from the static free path; a free followed by a matching later allocation must be observed.
Do not enable the proposed runtime discriminator by changing the research manifest.
conclusion: Explicit-buffer factory 0x825184D0 reaches creator 0x82533DB8 through device vtable 0x8204A1B0 slot +0x08 at pre-call boundary 0x82518608, with config words +0x00, +0x04, and +0x40 in r4, r5, and r7, fixed r6=1, and fixed r8=0; 0x8251860C is only the call continuation. The creator builds a 0x34-byte header, executes allocator instructions 0x82533E98 and 0x82533EB0 with continuations 0x82533E9C and 0x82533EB4, and reaches the physical allocator path 0x8280DAC0 -> 0x8280DE40 -> MmAllocatePhysicalMemoryEx 0x82E92654, because attribute bit 31 of 0xBCFF0000 is set; bit 30 is clear, so the backing is not zero-filled. Refcount-zero cleanup reaches classifier call 0x82518B60 and post-call continuation 0x82518B64; for the accepted device vtable, classifier codes 3, 17, 18, and 19 select exact manager targets 0x825348A8, 0x825349F8, 0x82534950, and 0x82533D10, while code 20 performs no indirect device release. The target bodies queue the header with its allocation attributes or return success; the deferred pass 0x82535298 then frees the backing through 0x82E29160 -> MmFreePhysicalMemory 0x82E92434 once the header is unbound and its fence has passed. Static code proves no allocation-generation token, backing contents producer, or address-reuse event. The alternate factory 0x82517EC0 now has a bounded runtime join to this shared creator but retains a distinct input map and ownership path; a default-off input/release observation plus bounded returned-range write tracking remains proposed, and a reuse observation is admissible once a free at the deferred pass is observed.
